subject: Climate & Environment
title: Solar Energy After Dark
description: A quick, practical guide to Solar Energy After Dark.

hook.text: The sun sets every evening. Critics love pointing out that solar doesn't work at night.

buildup.text: But concentrated solar plants store heat in molten salt that stays hot for hours.

discovery.text: The Gemasolar plant in Spain ran for 36 straight days — including nights — on stored heat.

twist.text: Battery prices dropped 90% in a decade, making nighttime solar storage practical everywhere.

climax.text: Pairing panels with batteries turns solar from a daytime source into an anytime source.

punchline.text: Solar doesn't stop at sunset. It just saves some for later.

quiz.question: How did the Gemasolar plant generate power at night?
options: By storing heat in molten salt

details.summary: Solar panels produce no power at night, but emerging technologies aim to extend solar energy around the clock. Battery storage, concentrated solar with thermal reserves.
details.whyItMatters: Intermittency is solar's biggest limitation. Solutions that deliver solar energy after sunset would make solar a more reliable baseload power source.
takeaways: Battery storage is the leading solution for nighttime solar
Concentrated solar plants store heat in molten salt for hours
Radiative cooling panels are an experimental nighttime concept

faq.question: How does concentrated solar power store energy?
faq.answer: Mirrors focus sunlight onto a receiver that heats molten salt to over 500 degrees Celsius. The stored heat drives steam turbines for hours after sunset. Plants like Gemasolar in Spain have demonstrated near-24-hour solar electricity generation.

faq.question: Can solar panels really work at night?
faq.answer: Researchers at Stanford developed experimental panels that generate small amounts of electricity by radiating heat into the cold night sky. Output is tiny compared to daytime generation, so practical nighttime solar remains dependent on storage technologies.
